texts.preamble: Mohd. Mian S/O Mohd. Faiyaz vs Food Inspector on 26 April, 2016 1 In The Court Of Sh. Rakesh Pandit, Asj-01, New Delhi District, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Ca No. 43/16 Mohd. Mian S/o Mohd. Faiyaz M/s Awami Co-operative Store 1807, Kalan Mahal, Jamma Masjid, Delhi R/o 1190, Kalan Mahal, Jamma Masjid, Delhi. ....App Vs. Food Inspector Department of Pfa Govt. Of Nct of Delhi A-20 Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035. .... Respo Date of receiving of Appeal : 04.04.2016 Date of arguments : 04.04.2016 Date of judgment : 26.04.2016 Judgment
texts.facts: 2 The brief facts of the case as per record and from trial court record are that accused is running an establishment namely M/s Awami Cooperative Store, 1807, Kalan Mahal, Jama Masjid, Delhi. On 07.07.2004 CA No. 43/16 Mohd. Mian Vs. State page 1 of 7 at about 6.00 p.m. Food Inspector Sh. Shyam Lal visited the said place and purchased 1500 grams of "Dal Arhar" (ready for sale) from accused. FI was accompanied with SDM/LHA Sh. N. R. Sharma The said Dal Arhar was purchased for the purposes of analysis under PFA Act. The same sample was divided into three parts, packed as per Rules of PFA. Panchanama was prepared. One sample was sent for analysis to Public Analyst. As per the report of Analyst, sample did not confirm to the standard because "The sample is adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz tartrazine. Mohd. Mian S/O Mohd. Faiyaz vs Food Inspector on 26 April, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88688147/ 1 3 As the sample was failed, prosecution was launched by Food Inspector by filing complaint dated 21.12.2004 with the court. Accused was summoned. He has not exercised his right u/sec.13(2) PFA Act and get the sample analyzed by CFL. 4 Charge was framed against accused u/sec.2(ia) (a) (j) (m) read with sec.7 of PFA Act, 1954 punishable u/sec.16(1A) of PFA Act. 6 In this appeal, the accused has assailed the judgment on the following grounds:- (i) Non-compliance of Sec.10(7) of PFA Act and Rule i.e. independent witnesses were not joined. (ii) Non-compliance of Rule 17 and 18 of PFA Rules i.e. CA No. 43/16 Mohd. Mian Vs. State page 2 the samples were not properly dispatched to public analyst and the sample seal was not sent. (iii) Non-compliance of Rule 14 of PFA Rules i.e. the bottles, jhawa, polythene were not made clean and dried at the spot by the food inspector or any other official. (iv) The public analyst took about 6 days to sign his report hence prejudice caused to appellant. (v) Tartrazine colour is permitted in food articles. 7 No reply was filed by respondent/state and the matter was argued orally.
texts.arguments: 9 It is argued by counsel for appellant that no public witness was present in the proceedings nor efforts were made and thus compliance of Sec.10 (7) PFA Act was not done. 10 It is further argued that there is non-compliance of Rule 17 and 18 of PFA rules i.e. the seal of the samples were not sent separately and not mentioned in the PA Report. It is further stated that the samples were not properly dispatched. I CA No. 43/16 Mohd. Mian Vs. State page 3 of 7 do not find any different opinion than as stated by the trial court and hence the arguments raised by the the counsel for appellant in this regard are rejected since the same are properly and correctly dealt by the trial court in the findings from para 90 to 96 in the judgment. 11 It is further argued that the PA report was not signed on the same date on which the analysis was done. It is stated that prejudice had caused to the accused as it caused delay and due to that reason the samples could not be sent for examination for CFL by the accused/appellant. As far as this argument is concerned, the same does not have any force as the adulteration is on account of "synthetic colour tartrazine". The said colour/sample is not a perishable item. This argument was also done by Ld. defence counsel before the trial court and was dealt by the trial court in CA No. 43/16 Mohd. Mian Vs. State page 4 of 7 para 105 of the judgment. However, this fact was elaborated further by Hon. Supreme Court in Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236 stating that "it must be the endeavour of the FI to use clean and dry CA No. 43/16 Mohd. Mian Vs. State page 5 of 7 implements in sampling the articles of food. If unhygienic methods are adopted, it will effect the result of analysis. So, the Hon. Supreme Court use the word "implements" instead of only "dry and clean bottles/containers". Similarly, in other judgments, i.e. State of Haryana Vs. Kishan Kumar CLT 559, it was observed that the prosecution had not stated that the "weighing scale" was clean. Similarly, in other judgments, like Sardar Mal Jain, 1996 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 203, it was stated that the newspaper on which the Barfi was weighed was not clean. Similarly, in Shashi Kant Vs. State of UP, 1983 (1) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases 90, it was observed that the "bhagona" was not proved to be clean and dry. 17 So, accordingly, it can be said that the law which can be crystallized from various judgments of Hon. High Courts as well as Hon. Supreme Court that if in evidence, the prosecution states that the sample commodity had touched a surface of an "implement", it is the duty of the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the said implement was clean and dry and thus could not have added any impurity to the sample.
